Article.ArticleTitle: Investigating the association between interferons and flares of systemic lupus erythematosus at a single cell level.

Abstract.AbstractText: Elevated levels of interferons (IFN) are a hallmark of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and are linked to disease flares, but the precise mechanisms underlying this remain unclear. We examined the association between IFN-stimulated proteins (ISPs) and immune changes in flaring and quiescent SLE patients at single-cell resolution.

Using CyTOF, six ISPs were measured in PBMC populations from 18 healthy controls, 24 quiescent SLE patients, and 46 recently flaring SLE patients. Individual ISPs and a composite ISP score were assessed.

Analysis of 29 immune populations revealed that mean ISP levels correlated with peripheral blood IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) expression and were higher in flaring than quiescent patients. Despite this correlation, ISP expression was heterogeneous between and within cell subsets. To identify factors contributing to this heterogeneity, we compared the top ISP-expressing cells with the remaining cells in each subject. High ISP-expressing cells had increased trafficking marker expression with distinct expression patterns suggesting that cells may have transited different tissues. Except for β7, these molecules were not induced by IFN in-vitro. Longitudinal analysis revealed that ISP expression gradually decreased in T and activated innate immune populations with flare resolution, whereas that in B cell populations remained stable with the baseline levels predicting sustained or recurrent disease activity one year later.

Although mean ISP expression in most cell populations correlated with global ISG expression, there is heterogeneity between and within immune populations in SLE, likely reflecting variable IFN exposure as cells traffic through inflamed sites within the body.

Article.ArticleTitle: Type I IFN promotes ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity in pre-clinical radiation-induced lung injury.

Abstract.AbstractText: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) is a common dose-limiting toxicity after radiotherapy for lung cancer, but the immunological mechanisms contributing to RILI pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Here we analyze a RILI mouse model using high-dose, restricted-field irradiation to the left lung. Flow cytometry and cytokine profiling analysis of innate lymphoid cells (ILC) reveals a radiation-induced shift from lung-resident type 2 ILCs (ILC2) toward pro-inflammatory type 1 ILCs (ILC1). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of mouse lung ILC populations after radiation suggests that type I interferon (IFN) promotes radiation-induced ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity. In vitro, IFN-β stimulation of mouse ILC2s leads to increased expression of the ILC1 markers T-bet and IFN-γ, while IFN-β stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells increases the ILC1-to-ILC2 ratio. In vivo, inhibition of type I IFN signaling attenuates lung damage after irradiation in our RILI model. Thus, our findings indicate that radiation-induced type I IFN induces ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity to contribute to RILI pathogenesis, and suggest that targeting type I IFN signaling may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate radiation-induced lung injury.

Article.ArticleTitle: Single-cell profiling of peripheral immune remodeling in BK polyomavirus-associated nephropathy after kidney transplantation.

Abstract.AbstractText: BK polyomavirus-associated nephropathy (BKPyVAN) remains a major cause of allograft dysfunction after kidney transplantation. To define peripheral immune signatures associated with distinct clinical states of BKPyV infection, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from kidney transplant recipients across three clinical states: stable graft function (n = 1), BKPyV DNAemia (n = 2), and biopsy-proven BKPyVAN (n = 3). We identified 17 immune cell populations and observed remodeling of both the innate and adaptive compartments. Monocyte subsets differed across clinical states, with CD16+ non-classical monocytes enriched in BKPyV DNAemia and inflammatory monocytes more abundant in BKPyVAN. CD8+ T-cell frequency was higher in BKPyVAN than in BKPyV DNAemia, while NK-cell frequency was lower in BKPyV DNAemia and BKPyVAN than in Stable, consistent with altered antiviral surveillance. A rare but transcriptionally distinct population, termed Activated Effector Cells (AECs), comprised only 0.60% of cells in BKPyVAN (104 of 17,238 cells) yet accounted for 12.15% of cluster-associated marker calls, the highest among the 17 populations, and displayed marked enrichment of cell cycle and RNA metabolic pathways. Across multiple lineages, AUC-based gene set enrichment analysis revealed convergent activation of RNA processing and intracellular transport pathways. Pseudobulk differential expression and permutation testing supported condition-associated transcriptional signatures, and leading-edge gene analysis identified candidate transcriptional readouts, including cell cycle regulators, inflammatory mediators, and RNA processing genes, with potential utility for blood-based monitoring. These findings reveal peripheral immune remodeling across the clinical states of BK polyomavirus infection and highlight the value of resolving rare, transcriptionally distinct immune populations, providing a rationale for noninvasive, transcriptomics-informed monitoring and risk stratification strategies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies CCDC69 as a marker associated with germinal center B-cell infiltration in TNBC: development and validation.

Abstract.AbstractText: Although coiled-coil domain containing 69 (CCDC69) has been implicated in tumor biology, its role in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and immune regulation remains unclear. Bulk transcriptomic data, single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, and spatial transcriptomics were used to investigate the role of CCDC69 in TNBC. Germinal center B-cell (GCB) signatures were quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and their associations with CCDC69 expression were assessed using correlation, ROC, and logistic regression analyses. An independent external TNBC cohort (GSE58812) was used to validate the association between CCDC69 expression, GCB infiltration, and survival outcomes. CCDC69 expression was significantly downregulated in breast cancer tissues but was associated with favorable survival outcomes in TNBC patients. CCDC69 expression positively correlated with multiple immune cell populations, particularly B cells and plasma cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated that CCDC69 expression was enriched in B-lineage cells, especially GCB. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further showed that CCDC69-high regions were spatially co-localized with B-cell-rich and germinal center-like immune niches. In the TCGA TNBC cohort, CCDC69 expression was strongly associated with GCB infiltration and effectively distinguished GCB-high tumors. Logistic regression analysis confirmed that CCDC69 was independently associated with GCB enrichment. Findings were validated in the GSE58812 cohort. CCDC69 expression correlated with GCB-related signatures, showed good discriminative performance in identifying GCB-high tumors, and was associated with improved patient outcomes when combined with GCB enrichment. CCDC69 is closely associated with B-cell-mediated immune responses and germinal center niches in TNBC. Our findings suggest that CCDC69 may serve as a robust biomarker of immune activation and favorable prognosis.

Article.ArticleTitle: Donor-aware integrative single-cell analysis distinguishes consistent memory B-cell programmes from donor-sensitive state boundaries in untreated rheumatoid arthritis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Single-cell transcriptomics resolves immune-cell heterogeneity, but whether cluster boundaries or coordinated programmes are the more transferable unit across donors remains uncertain. We reanalyzed 14,414 circulating memory B cells from four untreated rheumatoid arthritis donors. Harmony increased mean local donor entropy from 0.506 to 0.912, while original labels showed only moderate agreement with uncorrected and Harmony reclustering (adjusted Rand indices 0.508 and 0.473). Conditional label permutations and analyses based on pan-B-centred residuals or state-marker genes supported donor-level consistency for most major states, but identified C3-PECAM1 and the rare C10-IFN state as weakly specific or quality-control-sensitive. In training-only donor-held-out transfer, accuracy was 66.0-70.5% and adjusted Rand index was 0.432-0.525, indicating partial transfer rather than independent state recovery. Removal of DoubletFinder-predicted doublets preserved 15-20 of each state's top 20 pseudobulk markers and did not change programme rank order across states. Rank-based UCell scores agreed with AddModuleScore in both datasets. In an independent cohort of 5,725 memory B cells from 34 donors, adapted programme scores could be quantified, but no disease-activity or serological association remained significant after correction; treatment and unavailable disease-duration data limited clinical interpretation. These results distinguish recurrent donor-level transcriptional structure from analysis-sensitive state boundaries and support programme-level interpretation without claiming independent cell-state validation or biomarker utility.
